subject: Subject BR-027-0043 - LVEF Decrease at Week 20
body:
Hi Sarah,

I wanted to give you a heads up about Subject BR-027-0043. She came in for her Week 20 visit yesterday and we completed the protocol-required ECHO. Her LVEF came back at 48%, which is down from 62% at baseline.

Per protocol Section 6.4.2, this is a >10% absolute decrease from baseline, so we're holding trastuzumab per the dose modification guidelines. Patient is asymptomatic - no chest pain, no shortness of breath, no edema. Vitals are stable.

We'll repeat the ECHO in 3 weeks per protocol and I'll enter this in the AE log as Grade 2 LVEF decrease. Dr. Patel wants to review with cardiology before the next dose.

Let me know if you need anything else on this.

Best,
Jennifer

body:
Hi Sarah,

Attaching the ECHO report from Dr. Williams (our cardiology team). 

To answer your questions:

1. Patient mentioned she's been more tired than usual over the past 2-3 weeks, but she attributed it to work stress and caring for her mother. No chest pain, no SOB at rest. She did mention she's been avoiding the stairs at work because she "gets winded" but she thought that was just being out of shape. We didn't probe too deeply at the time because she brought it up casually during check-in.

2. She wasn't seen by cardiology yesterday. Dr. Patel reviewed the ECHO and is arranging a cardiology consult for early next week. He wanted to wait to discuss with cards before alarming the patient, but given the LVEF drop he's moving forward with the referral.

3. I'm entering the AE in EDC now. The ECHO was done 11/12, so that's the date of identification. For causality - should I mark this as possibly related or probably related? Trastuzumab is known for cardiac toxicity but she's been on it for 5 months without issues until now.

Let me know if you need anything else.

Jennifer

subject: Re: Subject BR-027-0043 - LVEF Decrease at Week 20
body:
Sarah,

I need to update you on this situation. Patient called last night around 6 PM complaining of increased fatigue and some mild shortness of breath when lying down. Dr. Patel had her come to the ER for evaluation out of caution.

She was admitted to the observation unit overnight for cardiac monitoring and additional workup. Repeat troponin was slightly elevated (0.08 ng/mL, ref range <0.04) but stable on repeat at 4 hours. BNP was 245 pg/mL (baseline was 45). ECG showed normal sinus rhythm, no acute changes. She was given IV Lasix 20mg once for mild lower extremity edema that developed.

Cardiology saw her overnight and confirmed mild heart failure, likely trastuzumab-related cardiomyopathy. They started her on lisinopril 5mg daily and recommended holding all trastuzumab permanently. She was discharged this morning with cardiology follow-up in 1 week.

I haven't updated the AE in EDC yet because I wanted to check with you first - this seems more serious now. Do I need to upgrade this to a Grade 3? And should this be reported as an SAE since she was hospitalized?

Patient is home now and doing okay. She's understandably upset about stopping treatment.

Jennifer

subject: Re: Subject BR-027-0043 - LVEF Decrease at Week 20
body:
Sarah,

I wanted to weigh in on this case as Jennifer has kept me updated. From a clinical perspective, this patient clearly developed trastuzumab-related cardiomyopathy. The timeline is consistent - progressive LVEF decline with symptoms developing over 2-3 weeks culminating in mild decompensated heart failure requiring hospitalization.

In my medical opinion, this is definitely related to study drug (probably related at minimum, possibly definitely related). The CTCAE grade is tricky - the LVEF drop itself might be Grade 2 (asymptomatic, >10-20% decrease), but once she developed symptomatic heart failure requiring hospitalization and initiation of heart failure therapy, I believe this crosses into Grade 3 territory.

I've permanently discontinued trastuzumab per protocol. She'll continue on just paclitaxel - though honestly at this point we're nearly done with the 12-week paclitaxel course anyway (she's on Week 20 of trastuzumab, so already past Week 12 of paclitaxel).

For reporting purposes, Jennifer is asking whether this meets SAE criteria given the overnight hospitalization. I believe it does, but I'll defer to you and your medical monitor on the regulatory reporting requirements. The hospitalization was for observation and medical management, not purely precautionary.

Please advise on next steps for reporting. I have all the source documentation ready if you need me to complete any forms.

Best regards,
Michael
